description: Curated ecological species knowledge base for HydraShield environmental restoration recommendations. This is REFERENCE KNOWLEDGE (literature-level ecological characteristics), not an observation. Every species entry carries sources and a confidence flag. Suitability for a concrete site is always flagged for local expert verification.

regions.mediterranean: Mediterranean-like conditions: hot, dry summers; mild winters; summer drought
regions.temperate: Temperate/Atlantic/Continental European conditions: no strong summer drought
regions.mountain: High-elevation conditions (applied as an additional constraint)

species.environmental_role: Native evergreen canopy oak; deep-rooted soil stabiliser; high biodiversity value (montado/dehesa systems).
species.fire_considerations: Very thick insulating cork bark gives mature trees documented survival of low-intensity fire; NOT fireproof — crown and young trees are vulnerable, and repeated severe fires kill stands.
species.post_fire_recovery: Strong epicormic resprouter after fire when the root collar survives.
species.management: Slow-growing; protect from overgrazing; cork stripping must follow regulations.
sources: Pausas et al., fire ecology of Mediterranean oaks (peer-reviewed)

species.environmental_role: Native evergreen oak; erosion control on slopes; key Mediterranean habitat species.
species.fire_considerations: Dense canopy can carry fire; mature trees resprout well. Lower flammability than resinous conifers but not fire-resistant in crown fire.
species.management: Tolerates poor soils; avoid waterlogged sites.

species.environmental_role: Native Iberian deciduous oak; supports diverse understorey; soil improvement.
species.fire_considerations: Deciduous hardwood with lower flammability than conifers; resprouts from the base.
species.management: Prefers some soil depth; mixed plantings recommended.

species.environmental_role: Native small tree/large shrub; pollinator and bird food source; understorey diversification.
species.fire_considerations: Documented vigorous post-fire resprouter; used in low-flammability landscape studies in southern France.
species.management: Tolerates pruning; useful in fuel-break edge design.
sources: Mediterranean firewise-landscaping research (e.g., SE France fuel-break studies)

species.environmental_role: Long-lived Mediterranean evergreen; deep roots; agroforestry value.
species.fire_considerations: Thick bark and low-resin foliage; comparatively low flammability in Mediterranean landscaping studies. Not fireproof.
species.post_fire_recovery: Can resprout from the trunk base after damage.
species.management: Slow to establish; frost-sensitive when young.

species.environmental_role: Iconic Mediterranean tree; agro-ecological mosaics that interrupt continuous wildland fuels.
species.fire_considerations: Low-flammability foliage relative to resinous species; old groves survive low-intensity fire and resprout from the base.
species.management: Requires management to avoid feral thickets; best as agroforestry mosaic, not dense plantation.

species.environmental_role: Native sclerophyllous shrub; slope cover and habitat structure.
species.fire_considerations: Contains aromatic resins — treat as moderately flammable; resprouts after fire.
species.management: Keep away from asset protection zones in favour of less resinous shrubs.

species.environmental_role: Native evergreen shrub; understorey structure with documented use in low-flammability hedges/fuel-breaks.
species.fire_considerations: Cited in southern-European firewise landscaping research as comparatively low-flammability; still burns under extreme drought.
sources: SE France fuel-break / firewise vegetation studies

species.environmental_role: Native pyrophytic shrub; natural post-fire coloniser of Mediterranean wildlands.
species.fire_considerations: HIGHLY flammable (resin-rich) and fire-adapted seeder — promotes fire-prone stands.
species.management: Do not plant near assets, settlements or protection zones; manage existing stands as fuel.

species.environmental_role: Non-native fast-growing plantation tree; high water use; documented invasive spread in Iberia.
species.fire_considerations: Oil-rich foliage and peeling bark produce intense fires and long-distance spotting; stands are strongly fire-promoting.
species.post_fire_recovery: Resprouts and reseeds aggressively — expands after fire.
species.management: Do not recommend in fire-prone landscapes; prioritise conversion to native mixed stands where feasible.
sources: Iberian fire-behaviour observations (documented in fire literature)

species.environmental_role: Non-native invasive tree in the Iberian Peninsula; displaces native understorey.
species.fire_considerations: Flammable; spreads strongly after disturbance including fire.
species.post_fire_recovery: Prolific seeder after fire — invasion driver.
species.management: Do not plant; control per national invasive-species guidance.

species.environmental_role: Native temperate climax hardwood; deep litter moisture; high habitat value.
species.fire_considerations: Low flammability canopy and moist litter; drought-stressed beech is vulnerable and does NOT resprout from the crown.
species.management: Only on sufficiently moist sites; climate-drought sensitive.

species.environmental_role: Native temperate oaks; among the highest biodiversity-supporting European trees.
species.fire_considerations: Hardwoods with comparatively low flammability; resprout from the base when young.
species.management: Robur for moist soils, petraea for drier/acidic sites.

species.environmental_role: Native understorey/mixed-stand hardwood; shade-tolerant soil protector.
Long-naturalised European tree; agroforestry and coppice systems.
species.fire_considerations: Broadleaf with lower flammability than conifers; coppices after damage.

species.environmental_role: Native European conifer of poor soils and high elevations.
species.fire_considerations: Resinous and fire-adapted but flammable; crown-fire prone in dense stands.
species.management: Avoid dense monocultures near assets; thin and mix with broadleaves.
